Brother '''Guy J. Consolmagno''', [[Society of Jesus|SJ]] (born September 19, 1952), is an American research [[astronomer]], [[physicist]], [[Jesuit]], and retired director of the [[Vatican Observatory]], and president of the Vatican Observatory Foundation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vofoundation.org/board-of-directors/|publisher=Vatican Observatory Foundation|title=Vatican Observatory Foundation Board of Directors|access-date=29 April 2020|archive-date=15 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200815105755/https://www.vofoundation.org/board-of-directors/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Life==
Consolmagno attended the [[University of Detroit Jesuit High School]] before he obtained his S.B. (1974) and S.M. (1975) degrees at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] and his Ph.D. (1978) at the [[University of Arizona]]'s [[Lunar and Planetary Laboratory]], all in [[planetary science]]. After postdoctoral research and teaching from 1978 to 1980 at [[Harvard College Observatory]] and from 1980 to 1983 at MIT, in 1983 he joined the US [[Peace Corps]] to serve in [[Kenya]] for two years, teaching astronomy and physics.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1063/PT.6.6.20170919a|title=Guy Consolmagno|journal=Physics Today|date=September 17, 2017|issue=9 |article-number=5837 |doi-access=free|bibcode=2017PhT..2017i5837. }}</ref> After his return he took a position as Assistant Professor at [[Lafayette College]] in [[Easton, Pennsylvania|Easton]], [[Pennsylvania]].

In 1989 he entered the [[Society of Jesus]], and took [[Monastic vows|vows]] as a brother in 1991. On entry into the order, he was assigned as an astronomer to the [[Vatican Observatory]], where he also served as curator of the Vatican Meteorite collection until his appointment as Foundation president in 2014. In addition to his continuing professional work in planetary science, he has also studied [[philosophy]] and [[theology]].

His research is centered on the connections between [[meteorites]] and [[asteroids]], and the origin and evolution of small bodies in the [[Solar System]]. In addition to over 70 refereed scientific papers, he has co-authored several books on [[astronomy]] for the popular market, which have been translated into multiple languages. During 1996, he took part in the Antarctic Search for Meteorites, [[ANSMET]], where he discovered a number of meteorites on the ice fields of Antarctica. An asteroid was named in his honour by the International Astronomical Union, [[International Astronomical Union|IAU]] in 2000 - [[4597 Consolmagno]].

He believes in the need for [[science]] and [[religion]] to work alongside one another rather than as competing ideologies. In 2006, he said, "Religion needs science to keep it away from superstition and keep it close to reality, to protect it from [[creationism]], which at the end of the day is a kind of [[paganism]] &ndash; it's turning [[Christian God|God]] into a [[nature god]]."<ref>{{cite news|url= https://www.scotsman.com/news/world/creationism-dismissed-kind-paganism-vaticans-astronomer-2508334|title= Creationism dismissed as 'a kind of paganism' by Vatican's astronomer|accessdate= 2017-11-25|archive-date= 2020-11-12|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20201112034502/https://www.scotsman.com/news/world/creationism-dismissed-kind-paganism-vaticans-astronomer-2508334|url-status= live}}</ref> Consolmagno was the chair of the [[Division for Planetary Sciences]] of the [[American Astronomical Society]],<ref>[http://www.aas.org/dps/officers.html Current Division of Planetary Science Officers] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060617060357/http://www.aas.org/dps/officers.html |date=2006-06-17 }} at aas.org</ref> serving from October 2006 to October 2007. In 2025 he began a two year term as president of [[The Meteoritical Society]].

Consolmagno is a popular speaker as well as a writer of popular science. He has been a guest of honor at several science fiction conventions, including [[DucKon]] in 2000, [[ConFusion (convention)|ConFusion]] in his native state of Michigan in 2002, [[Boskone (convention)|Boskone]] in 2007, [[ConClave (convention)|ConClave]] in 2009, MuseCon in 2015, and [[Minicon]] and [[NASFiC]] in 2017. He was an invited participant in [[Science Foo Camp|Scifoo]] in 2008 as well. He taught at Fordham University in New York City for the fall term of 2008. Consolmagno gave the keynote speech at the 2013 Stellafane amateur telescope making convention on Aug 10. 
He appeared on ''[[The Colbert Report]]'' in December 2009 to promote his book, ''The Heavens Proclaim''.<ref>[http://www.colbertnation.com/the-colbert-report-videos/257718/december-01-2009/gold--frankincense-and-mars---guy-consolmagno Gold, Frankincense and Mars] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100218150909/http://www.colbertnation.com/the-colbert-report-videos/257718/december-01-2009/gold--frankincense-and-mars---guy-consolmagno |date=2010-02-18 }}, December 1, 2009. The Colbert Report</ref> In May 2014, Consolmagno received an honorary doctorate (Doctor of Humane Letters, ''Honoris Causa'') from [[Georgetown University]] and spoke at the [[Georgetown College (Georgetown University)|Georgetown College]] commencement ceremony.<ref>{{cite news |url= http://www.georgetown.edu/hoyas2014/speakers.html |title= Georgetown Announces Speakers for 2014 Commencement |date= May 1, 2014 |work= Georgetown University |accessdate= May 1, 2014 |url-status= dead |archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20140502033259/http://www.georgetown.edu/hoyas2014/speakers.html |archivedate= May 2, 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://governance.georgetown.edu/honorary-degrees-list|title=Honorary Degree Recipients|website=governance.georgetown.edu|language=en|access-date=2017-04-17|archive-date=2017-01-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170118130805/http://governance.georgetown.edu/honorary-degrees-list|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2010, he was a guest on ''[[On Being]]'' with [[Krista Tippett]], alongside his friend and colleague Father [[George Coyne]], S.J. In the interview, Consolmagno and Coyne discussed their distinct and intimate relationships with science and faith. The show aired for a second time in 2011, and for a third time in September 2015.<ref name="On Being with Krista Tippett">{{cite web |url= http://www.onbeing.org/program/asteroids-stars-and-love-god/transcript/551 |title= Guy Consolmagno and George Coyne - Asteroids, Stars, and the Love of God |website= On Being with Krista Tippett |accessdate= September 20, 2015 |archive-date= September 28, 2015 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150928163847/http://www.onbeing.org/program/asteroids-stars-and-love-god/transcript/551 |url-status= dead }}</ref>

On July 2, 2014, he was awarded the [[Carl Sagan Medal]] for outstanding communication by an active planetary scientist to the general public by the [[Division for Planetary Sciences]] of the American Astronomical Society.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://dps.aas.org/news/aas-division-planetary-sciences-announces-2014-prize-winners |title=2014 AAS Prize Winners |accessdate=July 3, 2014 |archive-date=August 8, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160808224348/https://dps.aas.org/news/aas-division-planetary-sciences-announces-2014-prize-winners |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Known as the "pope's astronomer," he was named by [[Pope Francis]] to be the director of the [[Vatican Observatory]] in September 2015.<ref name="popesastronomer">{{cite news|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/talking-science-and-god-popes-new-chief-astronomer|title=Talking science and God with the pope's new chief astronomer|last=Cartlidge|first=Edwin|date=29 September 2015|work=[[Science (journal)|Science]]|accessdate=20 December 2015|archive-date=26 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211226025415/https://www.science.org/content/article/talking-science-and-god-popes-new-chief-astronomer|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url= http://www.catholicnews.com/services/englishnews/2015/pope-names-us-jesuit-to-head-vatican-observatory.cfm |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20151222114824/http://www.catholicnews.com/services/englishnews/2015/pope-names-us-jesuit-to-head-vatican-observatory.cfm |url-status= dead |archive-date= December 22, 2015 |title= Pope names U.S. Jesuit planetary scientist to head Vatican Observatory |accessdate= September 18, 2015}}</ref>

In 2022, Consolmagno was awarded the [[Society of Catholic Scientists|St. Albert Award]] by the Society of Catholic Scientists.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://catholicscientists.org/st-albert-award/ | title=St. Albert Award Archive | access-date=2022-08-24 | archive-date=2022-08-18 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220818230205/https://catholicscientists.org/st-albert-award/ | url-status=live }}</ref>

Consolmagno additionally has made several appearances on [[EWTN]]'s original programming, most notably featuring prominently in the August 2021 ''EWTN Vaticano'' special episode "Inside the Vatican Observatory - Where Science Meets Faith."<ref>{{Citation |title=Vaticano - 2021-08-01 - Inside the Vatican Observatory - Where Science Meets Faith |date=2 August 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RFtQ7_SrfQc |language=en |access-date=2022-10-02 |archive-date=2022-10-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221002170117/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RFtQ7_SrfQc |url-status=live }}</ref>
